description:
Programme Overview

The Rhodes Scholarship is one of the world's oldest and most international postgraduate scholarships, established in 1902. It provides full financial support for outstanding students from around the world to pursue full-time postgraduate studies at the University of Oxford.

Key Objectives

  • Develop public-spirited leaders who will make a positive impact globally
  • Promote international understanding and peace through academic excellence
  • Identify and nurture young people with the potential to become leaders in their fields

Funding & Benefits

  • University fees: All course fees and college fees (100% coverage)
  • Stipend: Living allowance of £21,060 per year (£1,755 per month, 2026-27 rate)
  • Travel allowance: Round-trip airfare to/from UK
  • Health insurance: Comprehensive health coverage
  • Arrival allowance: Initial settling-in expenses
  • Tenable for 1-3 years depending on the length of the chosen postgraduate program

Eligibility Criteria

  • Age: Typically 19-25 by October 1 of the year of application (some constituencies have slight variations)
  • Academic background: Hold a Bachelor's degree with first-class or high upper second-class honors (or equivalent international qualifications)
  • Nationality/Residency: Apply through a specific constituency based on citizenship or country of legal residence
  • English proficiency: Meet the University of Oxford's English language requirements
  • Leadership potential: Demonstrate outstanding leadership qualities and a commitment to service

Global Constituencies

The Rhodes Scholarship is available through 26 constituencies worldwide, including the United States, Canada, Australia, India, Pakistan, East Africa, Southern Africa, West Africa, the Middle East, Europe, China, and more. You can only apply through one constituency.

Selection Criteria

  1. Literary and scholarly attainments: Academic excellence and intellectual ability
  2. Energy to use one's talents to the full: Physical vigor and involvement in sports or other activities
  3. Truth, courage, devotion to duty, sympathy for and protection of the weak, kindliness, unselfishness and fellowship: Moral force of character
  4. Moral force of character and instincts to lead: Public-spirited ambitions and leadership potential

Application Process

  1. Determine your constituency
  2. Check eligibility and deadlines
  3. Prepare application documents:
  • Proof of identity (passport or national ID)
  • Academic transcripts
  • Proof of degree
  • CV/Resume
  • Personal statement (1,000-word essay addressing the Rhodes criteria)
  • Letters of recommendation (at least 5-8 references)
  • English proficiency proof (TOEFL/IELTS scores or equivalent)
  • Photograph
  1. Submit application online through the official portal
  2. Attend interview
  3. Final selection

Timeline

MilestoneDate
Application opensJuly-August
Application closesSeptember-October (varies by constituency)
ShortlistingNovember
InterviewsNovember-December
Final notificationDecember-January
Arrival in OxfordSeptember

Official Application Portal

https://www.rhodeshouse.ox.ac.uk/scholarships/apply/

Contact

scholarships@rhodeshouse.ox.ac.uk

Important Notes

  • Approximately 100 scholarships awarded globally each year.
  • Deferrals are generally not permitted.
  • Most successful applicants have a first-class degree or equivalent (GPA 3.7/4.0 or above).

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: Varies by constituency (typically September-October). Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
